topics.name: Whole numbers
subtopics: Describe the real number system by distinguishing natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational and irrational numbers
Use prime factorisation of numbers to find LCM and HCF
Solve problems involving ratio and rate, and direct and indirect proportion
Financial contexts: profit, loss, discount, VAT, budgets, accounts, loans, simple and compound interest, hire purchase, exchange rates, commission and rentals

topics.name: Integers
subtopics: Revise calculations with all four operations with integers, including squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots
Revise commutative, associative and distributive properties, and additive and multiplicative inverses for integers
Solve problems in contexts involving multiple operations with integers

topics.name: Exponents
subtopics: Revise representing integers in exponential form and numbers in scientific notation; extend scientific notation to negative exponents
Revise laws of exponents: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), (a × t)^n = a^n × t^n, a^0 = 1
Extend laws of exponents to integer exponents: a^(−m) = 1/a^m
Perform calculations with all four operations using numbers in exponential form
Solve problems in contexts involving numbers in exponential form, including scientific notation

topics.name: Formal assessment: Assignment
subtopics: Assignment on whole numbers, integers and exponents

topics.name: Numeric and geometric patterns
subtopics: Investigate and extend numeric and geometric patterns in physical or diagram form, in tables and represented algebraically
Patterns not limited to a constant difference or ratio, including learners' own creations
Describe and justify general rules for observed relationships in own words or in algebraic language

topics.name: Functions and relationships
subtopics: Determine input values, output values or rules using flow diagrams, tables, formulae and equations
Determine, interpret and justify equivalence of descriptions presented verbally, in flow diagrams, tables, formulae, equations and graphs on a Cartesian plane

topics.name: Algebraic expressions
subtopics: Revise conventions for writing algebraic expressions; like and unlike terms; coefficients and exponents
Recognise and differentiate between monomials, binomials and trinomials

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on all Term 1 topics

sba: Assignment: whole numbers, integers and exponents

topics.name: Algebraic expressions
subtopics: Revise adding and subtracting like terms, multiplying and dividing monomials, binomials and trinomials, and substitution (including common and decimal fractions)
Multiply integers and monomials by polynomials; divide polynomials by integers or monomials
Product of two binomials and the square of a binomial
Factorise expressions with common factors, difference of two squares and trinomials x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c (a a common factor)
Simplify algebraic expressions and algebraic fractions using factorisation

topics.name: Algebraic equations
subtopics: Revise setting up, analysing and solving equations by inspection, additive and multiplicative inverses and laws of exponents
Use substitution in equations to generate tables of ordered pairs
Extend to solving equations using factorisation, including equations of the form: a product of factors = 0

topics.name: Graphs
subtopics: Revise analysing and interpreting global graphs: linear or non-linear, constant, increasing or decreasing, maximum or minimum, discrete or continuous
Features of linear graphs: x-intercept, y-intercept and gradient
Revise drawing global graphs and plotting ordered pairs on the Cartesian plane
Draw linear graphs from given equations and determine equations from given linear graphs

topics.name: Geometry of straight lines
subtopics: Revise and describe relationships between angles formed by perpendicular lines, intersecting lines and parallel lines cut by a transversal
Solve geometric problems using the relationships between pairs of angles

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on all Term 1 and Term 2 topics

sba: Investigation: on any ONE of the Term 2 topics, administered before teaching it

topics.name: Geometry of 2D shapes
subtopics: Revise definitions of triangles; investigate by construction the relationship between the exterior angle of a triangle and its interior angles
Revise definitions of quadrilaterals by sides, angles and diagonals: parallelogram, rectangle, square, rhombus, trapezium, kite
Investigate by construction the diagonals of rectangles, squares, parallelograms, rhombi and kites, and the interior angle sum of polygons
Establish through investigation the minimum conditions for congruent and similar triangles
Solve geometric problems involving unknown sides and angles using properties of triangles, quadrilaterals, and congruent and similar triangles

topics.name: Area and perimeter
subtopics: Use formulae and conversions between SI units to calculate perimeter and area of polygons and circles
Investigate how doubling any or all dimensions of a 2D figure affects its perimeter and area

topics.name: Data handling: collect, organise, summarise, represent, interpret, analyse and report data
subtopics: Pose questions on social, economic and environmental issues; select and justify sources and methods for collecting data; distinguish samples and populations
Organise numerical data and summarise with measures of central tendency and dispersion, including extremes and outliers; organise data by more than one criterion
Represent data: bar and double bar graphs, histograms with given and own intervals, pie charts, broken-line graphs and scatter plots
Critically read, interpret and compare two sets of data on the same issue
Analyse data collection methods, summaries of data, and sources of error and bias
Report data: conclusions, predictions, comparisons, error and bias, appropriate summary statistics and the role of extremes and outliers

topics.name: Probability
subtopics: Determine probabilities for compound events using two-way tables and tree diagrams
Determine probabilities of outcomes and predict their relative frequency in simple experiments
Compare relative frequency with probability and explain possible differences

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on all Term 3 topics

sba: Project: covers a combination of topics from Term 1 to Term 3; completed before the end of Term 3

topics.name: Geometry of 3D objects
subtopics: Revise properties and definitions of the 5 Platonic solids (faces, vertices, edges)
Recognise and describe the properties of spheres and cylinders
Use nets to make models of cubes, prisms, pyramids and cylinders

topics.name: Surface area and volume of 3D objects
subtopics: Use formulae and SI unit conversions to calculate surface area, volume and capacity of cubes, rectangular prisms, triangular prisms and cylinders
Investigate how doubling any or all dimensions of right prisms and cylinders affects their volume

topics.name: Transformation geometry
subtopics: Transform points, line segments and simple figures on a co-ordinate plane: reflection in the x-axis, y-axis or line y = x; translation; rotation about a given point
Identify the transformation of a point given the co-ordinates of its image
Use proportion to describe the effect of enlargement or reduction on area and perimeter
Investigate the co-ordinates of vertices of figures enlarged or reduced by a given scale factor

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Revision of Term 1 to Term 4 topics

topics.name: Formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Test on Term 1 to Term 4 topics
